entries.name: Ultima Worlds Online: Origin
entries.summary: EA cancelled Ultima Worlds Online: Origin, a planned sequel to Ultima Online.

sources.title: EA reduces staff

entries.check: GameSpot, 22 Mar 2001: EA said “the only game cancellation the company would confirm” was Ultima Worlds Online: Origin.
entries.note: The timeline uses GameSpot’s 2001 report year. Its 22 March report quotes EA’s confirmation but does not say when the game was cancelled.

entries.name: EA.com San Diego studio
entries.summary: EA announced the closure of its EA.com San Diego studio in a restructuring.

sources.title: Electronic Arts Inc. 2005 Form 10-K

entries.check: EA’s 2005 Form 10-K: “In October 2001, we announced restructuring initiatives involving EA.com and the closure of EA.com’s San Diego studio”
entries.note: EA’s 2005 Form 10-K dates its announcement to October 2001; it does not say when the closure took effect.

entries.name: EA Seattle studio
entries.summary: EA closed its Seattle studio while consolidating local development efforts in Redwood City and Vancouver.

sources.title: Electronic Arts Inc. 2005 Form 10-K

entries.check: EA’s 2005 Form 10-K: in fiscal Q3 2003 it “closed ... our studio located in Seattle, Washington” while consolidating local development efforts in Redwood City and Vancouver.
entries.note: The filing dates the closure to fiscal Q3 2003, which ended in December 2002; it gives no month or day.

entries.name: EA Bellevue studio (Manley & Associates lineage)
entries.summary: EA announced the closure of its Bellevue studio, moving about half its staff to Vancouver and laying off the rest.

sources.title: Electronic Arts closing Bellevue game studio

entries.check: Seattle Post-Intelligencer, 21 Oct 2002: the Bellevue office “opened in 1997 after Electronic Arts acquired Issaquah-based Manley & Associates”
entries.note: The Seattle Post-Intelligencer’s 21 October 2002 report says staff were told the previous week; October is the announcement month, not the closure date.

entries.name: EA Pacific
entries.summary: EA announced that virtually the entire EA Pacific team would continue at its new Los Angeles studio during the Westwood consolidation.

sources.title: EA consolidates studios, closes Westwood

entries.check: GameSpot, 30 Jan 2003: EA said virtually the entire EA Pacific team would continue at its new Los Angeles campus.
entries.note: GameSpot’s 30 January 2003 article reports EA’s announcement that the team would continue at EA Los Angeles; it does not establish when the transfer happened.

entries.name: Studio 33
entries.summary: EA acquired Studio 33 and said its Liverpool team would join the existing EA Northwest team.

sources.title: Electronic Arts Acquires Studio 33

entries.check: Nintendo World Report reproduces EA’s 16 Oct 2003 release: “the team of roughly 30 Liverpool-based employees will join the existing team at EA Northwest”.
entries.note: Nintendo World Report’s 16 October 2003 reproduction of EA’s release records the announced transfer, not when the team moved to EA Northwest.

entries.name: Westwood Studios
entries.summary: EA announced plans to close Westwood’s Las Vegas studio after significant layoffs, with transition staff staying until the planned March 31 closure.

sources.title: EA consolidates studios, closes Westwood

entries.check: GameSpot, 30 Jan 2003: EA announced plans for the “studio’s final closure on March 31” after significant layoffs at its Las Vegas studio.
entries.note: The date is GameSpot’s 30 January 2003 report of EA’s announcement; the planned 31 March closure is not confirmed as completed.

entries.name: Bullfrog Productions
entries.summary: Bullfrog’s remaining studio work was absorbed into EA UK.

sources.title: We See Farther - A History of Electronic Arts

entries.check: Game Developer says Bullfrog was “eventually absorbed into EA UK in 2004.”

entries.name: Origin Systems
entries.summary: EA closed Origin Systems’ Austin studio and moved staff who stayed with the company to Redwood Shores.

sources.title: Origin obit confirmed
Electronic Arts’ “workforce reduction” to axe 117 jobs

entries.check: GameSpot, 26 Feb 2004: EA planned to shutter Austin operations by the end of April; a June report confirmed the “closure of its Origin studio in Austin.”
entries.note: A later report confirmed the studio closure but did not give the final day, so only the year is recorded.

entries.name: Ultima X: Odyssey
entries.summary: EA ended development on Ultima X: Odyssey and moved its remaining team to other Ultima projects.

sources.title: Electronic Arts kills Ultima X: Odyssey

entries.check: GameSpot, 1 Jul 2004: “As of today, development on Ultima X: Odyssey has ended”

entries.name: Hypnotix
entries.summary: EA moved Hypnotix’s 35-person development team to its Tiburon studio to work on action-oriented games.

sources.title: Hypnotix Team Joins EA Tiburon

entries.check: Game Developer, 27 Jul 2005: Hypnotix’s “35 person-strong development team” “has joined EA's Tiburon” studio.
entries.note: Dated by the month of Game Developer’s report that the team had joined EA Tiburon; the report doesn’t give the day of the move.

entries.name: JAMDAT Mobile
entries.summary: EA merged its existing mobile game development and publishing business with JAMDAT after acquiring the company to form EA Mobile.

sources.title: GDC Mobile: The Future of Mobile Gaming and its Enemies
Electronic Arts Inc. 2006 Form 10-K

entries.check: EA’s 2006 Form 10-K: after acquiring JAMDAT in February, EA “merged our existing mobile business with JAMDAT to establish our EA Mobile business”; Game Developer places the merger about two months before 31 March.
entries.note: EA acquired JAMDAT on 15 February 2006 and says the merger came afterwards. Game Developer puts it about two months before 31 March 2006. Neither gives a month, so only the year is given.

entries.name: DICE Canada
entries.summary: EA announced it was closing its London, Ontario DICE branch and moving its in-development projects to the Stockholm studio.

sources.title: EA shuts down DICE Canada

entries.check: GameSpot’s 6 Oct 2006 report says EA confirmed the London, Ontario studio was “being closed,” with projects moved to Stockholm.
entries.note: The date is GameSpot’s 6 October 2006 report of EA’s closure announcement; the article does not date EA’s communication or give an effective date.

entries.name: EA Warrington studio
entries.summary: EA announced it was closing its Warrington studio and offering affected staff roles at other UK studios.

sources.title: Electronic Arts to close UK studio

entries.check: Game Developer’s 17 Oct 2006 report says EA confirmed it was “closing its Warrington studio” and offering affected staff roles at other UK studios.
entries.note: The date is Game Developer’s 17 October 2006 report of EA’s closure announcement; the article does not date EA’s communication or give an effective date.

entries.name: The Lord of the Rings: The White Council
entries.summary: EA cancelled The White Council in 2007, having described it publicly as on indefinite hiatus; a former executive producer later said the project was dead.

sources.title: Why EA Canceled The Lord Of The Rings: The White Council

entries.check: GameSpot, 9 Dec 2020: “When The White Council was canceled in 2007”; former executive producer Steve Gray called it “dead as a doornail.”
entries.note: GameSpot says it was “canceled in 2007”. It also says EA never officially cancelled it, and called it an indefinite hiatus.

entries.name: EA Japan studio
entries.summary: EA announced that its Japanese internal studio would close and move under EA Partners to work with external developers.

sources.title: EA closes Japan studio

entries.check: GameSpot’s 8 Feb 2007 report says the studio “will soon be closing its doors after three years” and “originally opened three years ago”.
entries.note: The date is GameSpot’s 8 February 2007 report quoting a planned closure; it does not date EA’s communication or establish when or whether the closure took effect.

entries.name: EA Chicago
entries.summary: EA announced it was closing its Chicago studio, which had worked on the Def Jam and Fight Night series.

sources.title: EA Chicago closing

entries.check: GameSpot, 6 Nov 2007: an internal memo said “EA Chicago is also being closed.”
entries.note: GameSpot’s 6 November 2007 article reports an internal memo announcing the closure; it gives no effective date.

entries.name: Tiberium
entries.summary: EA cancelled Tiberium, a Command & Conquer first-person shooter that was in development at its Los Angeles studio.

sources.title: Tiberium terminated

entries.check: GameSpot, 30 Sep 2008: EA confirmed the game “has been canceled outright” and suspended work “effective immediately”

entries.name: Pandemic Studios
entries.summary: A November 2009 report described EA’s shutdown of Pandemic Studios as under way, with about 200 laid off and the rest moved to EA Los Angeles.

sources.title: EA Shutters Pandemic Studios

entries.check: SoCalTech, 18 Nov 2009: “Electronics Arts is shutting down Los Angeles-based Pandemic Studios”; around 200 were laid off and the rest transferred.
entries.note: The date is SoCalTech’s November 2009 report of the shutdown under way; it does not establish when the studio finished closing.

entries.name: NBA Elite 11
entries.summary: EA cancelled NBA Elite 11 after delaying the basketball game for the 2010–2011 season.

sources.title: NBA Elite 11 canceled

entries.check: GameSpot, 2 Nov 2010: EA announced it had “canceled NBA Elite 11 outright.”
entries.note: GameSpot reports EA’s 2 November 2010 cancellation announcement; it does not separately date when development ended.

entries.name: EA Bright Light
entries.summary: EA closed its Guildford studio, which had opened as EA UK and later became Bright Light.

sources.title: EA switches off Bright Light studio
EA Bright Light shuttered – Report

entries.check: MCV, 5 Jan 2012: two people confirmed the studio “closed late last year.” GameSpot says EA opened the Guildford studio in 1995 as EA UK.
entries.note: MCV placed the closure in late 2011, likely mid-November; only the year is recorded.

entries.name: PopCap Dublin studio
entries.summary: PopCap closed its Dublin operations, eliminating 96 jobs at its European headquarters.

sources.title: PopCap closes Dublin office
PopCap shuts down Dublin studio
EA closes PopCap Dublin

entries.check: TheJournal.ie, 24 Sep 2012: “PopCap Games has closed its Dublin operations today,” affecting 96 jobs. MCV says it opened the Dublin studio in 2006 as its European HQ.

entries.name: NBA Live 13
entries.summary: EA Sports cancelled NBA Live 13 and said it would sit out the full basketball season.

sources.title: EA Sports Cancels NBA Live 13

entries.check: Kotaku, 27 Sep 2012: “EA Sports today canceled its troubled NBA Live 13 project.”

entries.name: Danger Close Games
entries.summary: EA disbanded Danger Close, the Medal of Honor studio; its staff left or moved to DICE and other EA teams.

sources.title: EA confirms Danger Close team disbanded

entries.check: MCV’s 14 Jun 2013 report quotes Patrick Söderlund saying: “Danger Close as it was doesn’t exist anymore,”
entries.note: The date is MCV’s 2013 report of Söderlund’s statement; it does not establish when the Danger Close team ceased to exist.

entries.name: EA Phenomic
entries.summary: EA Phenomic closed and laid off 60 employees, according to reports citing sources close to the studio.

sources.title: Report: Electronic Arts Closes Phenomic Studio

entries.check: Game Informer, 12 Jul 2013: GamesIndustry reported EA had “shuttered EA Phenomic,” and the article says the studio was founded in 1997.
entries.note: Game Informer reported that the studio had been shuttered and described it as part of EA studio closings conducted in 2013; it gave no more precise event date.

entries.name: BioWare San Francisco
entries.summary: A source inside BioWare San Francisco told GameSpot the studio had closed and laid off 25 to 30 employees.

sources.title: BioWare San Francisco closed – Report

entries.check: GameSpot, 5 Mar 2013: a source inside the studio said BioWare San Francisco “has been closed” and that 25 to 30 employees were laid off.
entries.note: Dated by the month of GameSpot’s report of 5 March 2013, from a source inside the studio; it doesn’t give the day of the closure.

entries.name: PopCap Vancouver office
entries.summary: PopCap closed its Vancouver development office, according to employee reports.

sources.title: EA Layoffs Hit Vancouver: PopCap and Quicklime To Close
EA shuts PopCap Vancouver, word Seattle offices

entries.check: GeekWire, 26 Apr 2013: PopCap employees said the office was “closed”; BCBusiness reported former EA employees said “the two studios had been shut down.”
entries.note: The timeline uses the April 2013 report month from GeekWire and BCBusiness; employee accounts do not give a closure day, and EA did not name the affected locations.

entries.name: Quicklime Games
entries.summary: EA closed Quicklime Games, its Vancouver development studio.

sources.title: EA Layoffs Hit Vancouver: PopCap and Quicklime To Close

entries.check: BCBusiness, 26 Apr 2013: former EA employees reported that “the two studios had been shut down”; the article identifies Quicklime as responsible for Need for Speed: World.
entries.note: Dated by the month of BCBusiness’s report, from former EA employees; it doesn’t give the day of the closure.

entries.name: EA Mobile Brazil
entries.summary: EA confirmed it had closed its São Paulo mobile game development studio in Brazil.

sources.title: EA demite funcionários e fecha estúdio no Brasil
EA monta estúdio de games para celular no Brasil

entries.check: UOL, 11 Apr 2013: EA’s press office “confirmou o encerramento do estúdio de desenvolvimento do Brasil.” Teletime reported EA opened its São Paulo mobile studio in 2008.

entries.name: Victory Games
entries.summary: Victory Games closed after EA cancelled its Command & Conquer game, according to employees cited by Kotaku.

sources.title: EA Cancels Command & Conquer

entries.check: Kotaku, 29 Oct 2013: employees of Victory Games were “tweeting that EA has shut the studio down.”
entries.note: Dated by the month of Kotaku’s report of 29 October 2013, from employees’ posts; it doesn’t give the day of the closure.

entries.name: Command & Conquer (2013 game)
entries.summary: EA cancelled the free-to-play Command & Conquer game after its closed alpha.

sources.title: EA Cancels Command & Conquer

entries.check: Kotaku, 29 Oct 2013: Victory Games’ blog said EA had decided to “cease production of this version of the game.”
entries.note: The date is the Victory Games announcement reported by Kotaku on 29 October 2013; it does not establish when development stopped.

entries.name: Mythic Entertainment
entries.summary: Game Informer reported EA’s announcement that it was closing Mythic Entertainment’s Fairfax location.

sources.title: EA Shutters Warhammer Online Developer Mythic

entries.check: Game Informer, 29 May 2014, quotes EA: “We are closing the EA Mythic location in Fairfax, Virginia,” and says the studio was founded in 1995.
entries.note: The date is Game Informer’s 29 May 2014 report quoting EA’s closure announcement; it does not date EA’s communication or give an effective date.

entries.name: Maxis Emeryville
entries.summary: EA closed Maxis's Emeryville studio and moved Maxis development to its other studios.

sources.title: EA is shutting down Maxis Emeryville, the studio that brought you SimCity and The Sims

entries.check: The Next Web, 4 Mar 2015: “EA today suddenly closed Maxis’ Emeryville office”

entries.name: Star Wars: Ragtag
entries.summary: EA reportedly cancelled Ragtag, Visceral’s Star Wars heist game, when it closed the studio in October 2017.

sources.title: Sources: EA Canceled A Star Wars: Battlefront Spinoff Last Year

entries.check: Kotaku, 21 Feb 2020: “In October 2017, EA shut down Visceral and canceled Ragtag”
entries.note: EA’s 2017 statement described a pivot; a later Kotaku report explicitly said Ragtag was cancelled in October 2017.

entries.name: Visceral Games
entries.summary: Kotaku reported that EA shut down Visceral Games, the Dead Space studio, in October 2017.

sources.title: Sources: EA Canceled A Star Wars: Battlefront Spinoff Last Year

entries.check: Kotaku, 21 Feb 2020: “In October 2017, EA shut down Visceral and canceled Ragtag”.
entries.note: Kotaku’s later report dates EA’s shutdown of Visceral to October 2017; it does not give a day.

entries.name: Star Wars: Viking
entries.summary: EA reportedly cancelled Viking, a planned Battlefront spin-off, in 2019 after deciding its release schedule was unrealistic.

sources.title: Sources: EA Canceled A Star Wars: Battlefront Spinoff Last Year

entries.check: Kotaku, 21 Feb 2020: based on six people familiar with EA, “Viking was no more” after executives rejected its timeline.
entries.note: The report places the cancellation in spring 2019 but does not give a day.

entries.name: Codemasters Cheshire
entries.summary: EA merged Codemasters Cheshire, its DiRT team, into Criterion Games to work on Need for Speed.

sources.title: Dirt team Codemasters Cheshire merged with Need for Speed studio Criterion

entries.check: VGC, 12 May 2022: the Cheshire team "has been integrated into" Criterion Games; "No redundancies have been made as a result of the move"
entries.note: Dated by the month of VGC’s report of 12 May 2022; it doesn’t give the day of the integration.

entries.name: Titanfall Legends
entries.summary: EA and Respawn reportedly cancelled Titanfall Legends, a single-player game set in the Apex Legends and Titanfall universe.

sources.title: Report: EA Cancels Unannounced Single-Player Titanfall Game Titled "Titanfall Legends"

entries.check: MP1st, 1 Feb 2023, citing Jason Schreier (Bloomberg) and three people familiar with the matter; EA did not announce it.
entries.note: MP1st published its report on 1 February 2023. The timeline records its report year; the source does not establish when the cancellation occurred.

entries.name: Battlefield Mobile
entries.summary: EA halted development on Battlefield Mobile before release, after testing it in a regional soft launch.

sources.title: EA scraps Apex Legends Mobile and Battlefield Mobile
Battlefield Mobile lead says 2042’s failure contributed to Mobile’s cancellation and his studio’s closure

entries.check: Game Developer, 1 Feb 2023: Battlefield Mobile was “being axed before it ever saw the light of day”; VGC later dated its cancellation to January 2023.

entries.name: Industrial Toys
entries.summary: EA closed Industrial Toys after cancelling Battlefield Mobile, the studio’s first-person shooter for phones.

sources.title: EA scraps Apex Legends Mobile and Battlefield Mobile
Battlefield Mobile lead says 2042’s failure contributed to Mobile’s cancellation and his studio’s closure

entries.check: VGC, 16 May 2023: Seropian co-founded Industrial Toys in 2012, and the “120-strong studio Industrial Toys was also closed down.”

entries.name: Star Wars FPS (Respawn)
entries.summary: EA stopped early development of Respawn's Star Wars first-person action game.

sources.title: A note from Laura Miele
EA has cancelled Respawn’s Star Wars first-person shooter

entries.check: VGC, 28 Feb 2024: “Electronic Arts has cancelled an in-development Star Wars first-person shooter at Respawn”
entries.note: VGC’s 28 February 2024 report dates EA’s cancellation announcement; it does not establish when the cancellation took effect.

entries.name: Ridgeline Games
entries.summary: EA announced Ridgeline’s wind-down, and its Battlefield campaign work continued under Criterion for Battlefield 6.

sources.title: A note from Laura Miele
EA shutters Battlefield dev Ridgeline Games, torches Respawn's unannounced Star Wars shooter
Former Battlefield 6 campaign lead is disappointed he and other devs were not properly credited in the new FPS after working tirelessly for 1 to 2.5 years, building the foundation
Battlefield Studios: Four teams, one groundbreaking game

entries.check: EA, 28 Feb 2024: “we’ll be winding down Ridgeline as a standalone studio in Seattle”; Game Developer, 29 Feb 2024: campaign work “is set to continue under the guidance of Criterion”; GamesRadar, 21 Oct 2025: it “was finished out by Criterion”; EA, 10 Oct 2025: “Battlefield 6 is out now”.
entries.note: EA dated the wind-down announcement, not its completion; Game Developer said the single-player work would continue under Criterion, and GamesRadar later reported Criterion finished the campaign for Battlefield 6.

entries.name: Origin
entries.summary: EA shut down its Origin PC client and store, which the EA app replaced.

sources.title: EA will shut down Origin later this year
Update your operating system for the EA app

entries.check: Game Developer, 21 Jan 2025, reported EA’s scheduled 17 April shutdown; EA Help later confirmed “Origin has shut down” by 1 May 2025.
entries.note: The timeline records the supported event year, 2025. EA scheduled 17 April, and EA Help confirmed shutdown by 1 May; those sources do not establish the exact completion day.

entries.name: Black Panther
entries.summary: EA cancelled Black Panther, the game Cliffhanger Games was developing.

sources.title: EA has cancelled its Black Panther game and closed its studio Cliffhanger Games

entries.check: VGC, 28 May 2025: "Electronic Arts has cancelled its Black Panther game and closed down the studio that was working on it."
entries.note: Dated by the month of VGC’s report of 28 May 2025, citing an internal EA email; it doesn’t give the day of the decision.

entries.name: Cliffhanger Games
entries.summary: EA closed Cliffhanger Games, the studio making its Black Panther game.

sources.title: EA has cancelled its Black Panther game and closed its studio Cliffhanger Games

entries.check: VGC, 28 May 2025: EA "has shut down Cliffhanger Games", per IGN and an internal email from Laura Miele seen by VGC. VGC says Cliffhanger Games was formed in 2021.
entries.note: Dated by the month of VGC’s report of 28 May 2025, citing IGN and an internal EA email; it doesn’t give the day of the closure.

entries.name: BioWare
entries.summary: EA announced it was closing BioWare and its Edmonton workspace after deciding not to continue early development of a new Mass Effect.

sources.title: Building EA's Next Chapter

entries.check: EA, 21 Oct 2026: "We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we're closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace."
entries.note: The date is EA’s 21 October 2026 closure announcement; EA does not give the day the closure took effect.

entries.name: Mass Effect (early development at BioWare)
entries.summary: EA announced it would not move forward with a small BioWare team’s early development of a new Mass Effect.

sources.title: Building EA's Next Chapter

entries.check: EA, 21 Oct 2026: a small team at BioWare was "working on early-development for Mass Effect"; EA decided "not to move forward with this development".
entries.note: The date is EA’s 21 October 2026 announcement of its decision; it does not identify when development stopped.

entries.name: Harry Potter MMO
entries.summary: A former EA product marketing director said EA cancelled a Harry Potter MMO after it reached beta.

sources.title: EA Canceled A Harry Potter MMO, Apparently

entries.check: GameSpot, 27 Dec 2021: Kim Salzer said the game reached beta and “EA eventually pulled the plug.”
entries.note: The account came from a former EA product marketing director; it does not date the cancellation.

entries.name: Star Wars open-world game (Orca)
entries.summary: EA reportedly cancelled Orca, EA Vancouver’s open-world Star Wars project, after rebooting it from the Visceral game Ragtag.

sources.title: EA Cancels Open-World Star Wars Game
Sources: EA Canceled A Star Wars: Battlefront Spinoff Last Year

entries.check: Kotaku, 15 Jan 2019: “Now, that project is canceled, too”; its 21 Feb 2020 follow-up says Orca was “in development all throughout 2018” until cancellation and that it broke the news “last year.”
entries.note: Kotaku says Orca was in development throughout 2018 and reported its cancellation on 15 January 2019. Neither report dates EA’s decision, which may fall in either year.
